package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner;

import net.officefloor.plugin.variable.Val;
import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model.Owner;
import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.repository.OwnerRepository;
import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.escalation.DuplicateTelephoneException;

public class EnsureOwnerTelephoneUnique {

    public void service(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository ownerRepository)
            throws DuplicateTelephoneException {
        boolean taken = ownerRepository.findAll().stream()
                .anyMatch(other -> other.getTelephone() != null
                        && other.getTelephone().equals(owner.getTelephone()));
        if (taken) {
            throw new DuplicateTelephoneException("Telephone is already used by another owner");
        }
    }
}

I added email uniqueness enforcement mirroring the existing telephone-unique pattern, keeping structural impact minimal — all new small classes, plus a two-line wiring insert into the POST pipeline:

- **`EnsureOwnerEmailUnique`** — a new single-method function (CC 2, no surrounding class complexity) that throws when the owner's email (already lower-cased by `Owner.setEmail`) matches any other owner's.
- **`DuplicateEmailException`** — checked exception so it surfaces in the `throws` clause.
- **`DuplicateEmailExceptionHandler`** — responds **409 Conflict** with a `ProblemDetail`.
- **`DuplicateEmailException.yml`** escalation mapping.
- **`owners.POST.yml`** — inserted the `ensureUniqueEmail` step (under `transaction` governance) between telephone and household checks.

No existing function bodies were grown; the only edit to an existing file is the YAML wiring. The `coreRejectsDuplicateEmail` acceptance test and the full suite pass.
